narrative.overview:
Aevrik is a compact Windows-operate interface for inspecting a local development stack. Its visual language is instrument-like: neutral layered surfaces, aligned data, a persistent master/detail workspace, and a restrained iris signal for selection, focus, and action. The browser artifact uses Windows-oriented proportions and Segoe UI rather than a marketing dashboard vocabulary.

The dark graphite preview is the primary expression; the pearl light theme preserves the same hierarchy with lighter surfaces. The name and palette are agent-proposed working choices, not a final brand approval.
keyCharacteristics: Graphite/pearl neutral layers with one iris accent
Reversible preview controls and explicit simulated states

rules.name: The Signal Rule
rules.body: Use iris for a functional signal, not a broad decorative fill.

rules.name: The Labelled Status Rule
rules.body: Pair status color with words or a control state; color alone does not carry operational meaning.

rules.name: The Data Font Rule
rules.body: Use the monospace face only for technical values, never ordinary interface prose.

rules.name: The Instrument Panel Rule
rules.body: Keep the working list and properties pane in one surface whenever the viewport permits.

rules.name: The Quiet Depth Rule
rules.body: Use surface changes and hairline dividers internally; reserve shadow for floating boundaries.

dos: Use compact labelled operational controls and readable technical data.
Preserve visible focus, reduced-motion behavior, and text alongside status colors.
Keep sample state distinct from a native engine or live machine state.
donts: Do not reintroduce green branding, SaaS chrome, marketing heroes, or decorative metric cards.
Do not use iris as a generic decorative wash or make color the only status cue.
Do not promote simulated caption controls into native window behavior.
Do not canonize invented kickers/eyebrows, hard offset shadows, glyph icons, or display-face styling; none are part of this shipped system.
